completion_reason: Material integration decisions remain around failover identity, canonical persistence, and remote-provider data boundaries.

questions.label: Failover identity
questions.context: A failed endpoint automatically routes to the next queue object.
questions.question: What identity should carry across provider failover?

choices.text: Keep one run ID, create a new immutable attempt, and reuse the idempotency key.
Create a new run for every provider attempt and link them as retries.
Resume the same attempt on the next provider from its latest checkpoint.

questions.label: Canonical storage
questions.context: NexusCentral must own crash-safe context, checkpoints, and artifacts.
questions.question: What persistence boundary should be canonical?

choices.text: Transactional local metadata store plus content-addressed artifact files.
One relational database containing metadata and artifact payloads.
A required external storage service for all canonical state.
A pluggable storage interface from the first release.

questions.label: Remote data
questions.context: LAN mesh and PeerJS providers may cross machine or trust boundaries.
questions.question: What data may remote providers receive?

choices.text: Only an explicit scoped input bundle allowed by the queue group.
The full conversation or workflow context needed by the selected model.
Only prompt text; remote providers cannot receive files or memory.
Use the same unrestricted payload contract as direct endpoints.
